subject: Archaeology
subcategory: Lost Cities of the Ancient World
title: Palmyra: Pearl of the Desert
description: A short lesson to help you apply Palmyra: Pearl of the Desert.

hook.text: Palmyra was a Roman trading city in the Syrian desert ruled briefly by a queen who defied an emperor.

buildup.text: Queen Zenobia declared independence from Rome in 270 CE and conquered Egypt before Rome crushed her revolt.

discovery.text: Its colonnaded streets, temples, and tombs survived 1,700 years of abandonment in remarkable condition.

twist.text: In 2015, ISIS destroyed the Temple of Bel and other monuments, erasing what centuries of neglect could not.

climax.text: 3D scans made before the destruction are now being used to digitally reconstruct what was lost.

punchline.text: A queen defied Rome and lost. A city defied time and almost won.

quiz.question: What happened to Palmyra's ancient monuments in 2015?
options: An earthquake damaged several major structures
ISIS destroyed the Temple of Bel and other monuments
Flooding from a nearby dam submerged part of the ruins
